deadline.value: Advertised projects each set their own deadline, and you can also apply at any time with your own proposal.
deadline.quote: There are two main routes to undertaking a research project at Strathclyde - either by applying for an existing project or pursuing your own specific areas of interest. | You can apply at any time – all you have to do is pick your course and submit your application.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: You can name a supervisor in your application, but an offer follows only once a second supervisor is confirmed.
supervisor.quote: As soon as a second supervisor is confirmed, an offer will be sent to you through Pegasus, our online application system.

also.quote: Research supervisors are assigned to you by the Department of Computer & Information Sciences.

funding.value: Listed projects mix funded and unfunded places, and JARSS studentships are awarded by competition.
funding.quote: Funding: unfunded Information & sensation | Funding: funded John Anderson Research Studentship Scheme (JARSS)

also.quote: The JARSS 2026/27 competition will open in November 2025 and students successful in this competition will commence studies in October 2026.

entry_route.value: The stated entry is an honours degree; the University's general page says research applicants normally have a Masters, so check with the department.
entry_route.quote: We look for a first-class or upper second-class UK Honours degree, or overseas equivalent, in a computer science, mathematical, information science, or related discipline from a recognised academic institution.

also.quote: If you wish to apply for a research degree you'd normally have to have a Masters degree and some experience of research work.

ielts_min.value: The computing page asks for an IELTS score of 6.5 if English is not the first language.
ielts_min.quote: If English isn't your first language, you'll also need to have an IELTS score of 6.5 as proof of English proficiency.

notes: Artificial intelligence and data science appear as a research area here, not as a separate PhD, so no datasci record.
